metaDescription: Six large 10 L and 15 L ultrasonic cleaners under $150, compared on watts, heater, degas and gentle modes so you pick the right workshop tank.
introParagraphs: Once the budget stretches this far, ultrasonic cleaners stop being jewelry gadgets and become small workshop machines. The picks here hold 10 L to 15 L, which means whole carburetors, brake parts, tool sets and trays of hardware fit in a single batch. That capacity changes what matters: stated wattage, heater strength, a drain and a handle become more important than a pretty preset menu.

The catch is that bigger tanks spread power thinner and bring weight. A full 15 L tank is heavy, needs a sturdy bench and ideally a sink nearby, and several listings leave out heater wattage or tank dimensions entirely. Our job here is to sort which machines give clear, comparable numbers and which leave you guessing.

We evaluated each model from its product page specs and buyer feedback, not from claimed bench testing. Use the pick notes to find a match for your parts, then check the sections on watts per liter, degas and gentle modes, and what an even larger budget would add.

products.name: VEVOR 10L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 600W Heat, Gentle
products.description:
This 10 L VEVOR is the most complete machine in the group. Four transducers spread cavitation across a large tank, a 600W heating system warms the bath to 80 C quickly, and an upgraded degas step clears trapped air before cleaning starts. A gentle mode lets you step down for lighter items, which is rare at a workshop size.

It is more machine than a household needs for a few rings or one pair of glasses, and 40 kHz remains aggressive for soft stones and glued items. A full tank is heavy and wants a solid shelf or bench. The listing mentions a built-in drain, which saves lifting 10 L of dirty fluid to empty it.

In practice the drain and the large heater make weekly use pleasant. Against the 10 L knob-control VEVOR it adds a stated heater wattage, and against the 180W model it adds both heat transparency and degas. For most hobby garages it is the sensible default.
products.bestFor: Garage hobbyists who want strong heat, degas, a gentle option and a drain.

products.name: VEVOR 15L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 360W, 400W Heater
products.description:
For raw numbers this is the standout: six 60W transducers add up to 360W at 40 kHz, and a listed 400W heater warms the solution to speed up grease removal. The product page states a 10.6 x 8.7 x 4.1 inch maximum workpiece size, so you can check whether a part fits before ordering. A digital panel sets time up to 30 minutes and heat up to 80 C.

The tank is 5.9 inches deep, so tall items have to lie flat, and the listing text mentions no degas or gentle mode. Full power is a harsh match for fine jewelry or circuit boards. Plan on a sturdy bench because the footprint is large.

The 360W-with-degas VEVOR 15 L offers a gentler path, while this one gives you the clearest published spec sheet. Compared with the 240W 15 L unit it has half again as much ultrasonic output, which matters most for greasy loads.
products.bestFor: Workshop users cleaning greasy engine and machine parts who value published specs.

products.name: VEVOR 15L Sonic Cleaner, 360W, Degas and Gentle
products.description:
This 15 L VEVOR matches the strongest machine on ultrasonic watts but adds the two modes that make it safer to use. Degassing helps cavitation reach inside crevices and bores, and gentle mode lets the 360W unit step down for finer, thinner items. The listing also highlights a drainage feature and says both the chamber and basket are corrosion-resistant 304 stainless.

The text we had gives no heater wattage, so confirm that before buying if warm-up speed matters. Hot water at up to 80 C is unsafe for plastics and glued items, and a full-size 15 L unit needs a sturdy bench and a nearby sink to drain.

It costs you the published heater and tank dimensions that the other 15 L model with 400W provides. In exchange you get the degas and gentle controls that machine lacks, which makes this the better pick if your loads vary between sturdy parts and lighter pieces.
products.bestFor: Mixed workloads where some parts are robust and others need a softer touch.

products.name: VEVOR 10L Cleaner, Knob Control, Degas, Dual Power
products.description:
A single knob sets time and temperature on this 10 L VEVOR, so there is no menu to learn and no tiny screen to read. Dual power settings cover delicate items and heavier parts alike, and the degas mode is said to lift efficiency by 30 percent on trapped air. A scratch-proof basket and a cleaning ball come in the box.

Wattage for the transducers and heater is not stated, so power is hard to compare with the others. At 40 kHz it is still strong on soft stones and glued jewelry, and a full tank is heavy even with the upgraded lifting handle.

It is the friendliest of the 10 L models for someone who just wants to turn a dial. If you like numbers on the page, the 600W-heater model from the same maker is easier to judge. If you like simplicity, this one asks the least of you each time you start a cycle.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a physical knob and two power levels over screens and menus.

products.name: VEVOR 10L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W, Digital Display
products.description:
This model gives a plain 180W ultrasonic rating, which makes the cleaning power easy to judge against others. Multi-layer piezoelectric transducers aim for even vibration in the tank, and preset modes mean you do not have to guess time and temperature. An upgraded handle helps with lifting and moving the unit when it is full.

On paper 180W is modest for a 10 L tank holding greasy or heavy parts, and the listing mentions no gentle or degas mode for fine items. The heater wattage is not stated, so warm-up time is hard to compare.

It makes sense for lighter jobs such as small hardware batches, where the presets do the thinking. Next to the 360W 15 L models it is clearly a step down in force, but it also takes less room and costs less to fill. Pick it when you want a defined rating without paying for the biggest tank.

products.name: VEVOR 15L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 240W, Digital Display
products.description:
The 240W 15 L VEVOR is the entry to the large-tank class in this group. It outputs 240W at 40 kHz, with heating adjustable from 0 to 80 C and a digital display. A stainless tank and included basket keep items off the walls and floor, and an upgraded handle is meant to ease moving a liquid-filled tank.

It carries the lowest ultrasonic output of the large machines, so heavy grease or a full load may need a second cleaning cycle. The listing does not mention degas or gentle modes, and 40 kHz is rough on delicate things.

Choose it when you want 15 L of room for bulky pieces but your jobs are light, since 240W against the 360W units means slower results. If you regularly clean heavily soiled parts, the 360W models make that extra spend worthwhile, and if you value gentle modes the degas model is the better route.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Total ultrasonic watts only mean something relative to the liquid they are shaking. The 15 L models range from 240W to 360W, which is 16 versus 24 watts per liter, while the 10 L 180W unit works out to 18. Aim for the higher end if you clean greasy parts. A big tank with low watts simply cleans more slowly.

Warm solution loosens oil far faster than cold, but a weak heater can take a long time to warm a big tank. The 10 L VEVOR lists 600W and the 15 L VEVOR lists 400W, both reaching 80 C, while several others give no heater wattage. If warm-up time matters, favour a stated figure. Never heat plastics or glued assemblies.

Degassing clears trapped air from fresh fluid so cavitation reaches blind holes and crevices, and the knob-control 10 L says it lifts efficiency by 30 percent. Gentle mode lowers output for thin or delicate items. Only the 600W 10 L and the 360W degas 15 L offer both clearly. If you clean mixed loads, these modes are worth more than a few extra watts.

Ten liters of water weighs about ten kilograms before the parts go in, and fifteen liters is heavier still. A drain avoids lifting it, and handles help when moving a unit. The 600W 10 L and the degas 15 L both highlight drainage. Put the machine on a sturdy bench near a sink, never on a thin shelf.

Headline litres can mislead because items sit in a basket and tall pieces may not submerge. The 400W 15 L publishes a 10.6 x 8.7 x 4.1 inch work limit within a 5.9 inch deep tank, which is the clearest guide in the lineup. Measure your largest part first. Models labelled 10L-class or 15L-class give only approximate volume.

Every unit here runs 40 kHz, which is well suited to metal parts, nozzles and carburetors but rough on soft stones, glued jewelry, circuit boards and coated finishes. Check plating and coatings before a heated cycle, since heat can lift paint or soften adhesives. For fragile items, pick a model with a gentle mode such as the 600W 10 L or the 360W degas 15 L.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ultrasonic output per liter
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared listed watts against tank volume. The 15 L VEVOR at 360W with six transducers leads on output, the 240W unit trails, and the 10 L 180W model sits between them. Models with no wattage were flagged as harder to judge.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heating capability
howWeEvaluated.description: Heater wattage and range were read from the pages. The 10 L VEVOR with 600W heating leads, the 15 L with 400W follows, and others list only a 0 to 80 C range. Clarity of the spec counted as well as the number.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and mode flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We favoured machines that offer degas and gentle modes because they widen the safe range of items. The 600W 10 L and the degas 15 L led here, while single-mode units were scored as workshop tools only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: Large tanks are heavy, so handles and drain features were weighted. The 10 L with 600W and the 360W degas 15 L mention drainage, and most models note an upgraded handle. Unlisted features were not assumed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged what each machine adds relative to the others. The 600W 10 L is the most complete, the 400W 15 L has the clearest specs, and the 240W 15 L offers space at the lowest power. Scores reflect listing detail and buyer feedback only.

faq.q: Which large ultrasonic cleaner is best overall?
faq.a: The 10 L VEVOR with 600W heating is the most complete here, offering heat, degas, a gentle mode and a drain. If you want more raw output the 15 L at 360W with a 400W heater leads. Choose by your heaviest typical load.

faq.q: Is 360W enough for a 15 L tank?
faq.a: It is a respectable figure for a tank of that size and the highest in this guide. The 240W 15 L model works out lower per liter and may need a second cycle for heavy grease. More watts matter most for oil and carbon deposits.

faq.q: What does degas do and do I need it?
faq.a: Degassing runs the unit briefly to clear trapped air from fresh fluid so bubbles can form properly. It helps with blind holes and crevices, and the knob-control 10 L says it adds 30 percent efficiency. Machines without it can still clean, but may need an extra pass.

faq.q: Can I clean jewelry in these big machines?
faq.a: You can, but 40 kHz is aggressive for soft stones, glued pieces and fine settings, and most of these have no gentle mode. The 600W 10 L and the 360W degas 15 L offer one. For delicate jewelry a small high-frequency tub is a better tool.

faq.q: Do I need a special solution?
faq.a: Plain water can handle light dirt, but oil, carbon and rust respond better to a purpose-made solution at warm temperatures. Ultrasonics provide the agitation, not the chemistry. Check that the solution suits the metals and coatings on your parts.

faq.q: How heavy are these when full?
faq.a: Ten liters of liquid weighs roughly ten kilograms and fifteen liters weighs more, plus the machine and the parts. That is why handles and drains matter. Fill and empty with a sturdy surface and a sink nearby.

faq.q: Why do some listings omit wattage?
faq.a: Several VEVOR pages describe the capacity as 10L-class or 15L-class and skip ultrasonic or heater power. That makes comparison harder, so confirm specs before buying. The 180W, 240W and 360W models state their output plainly.
